external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment-status webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse the storefront and place orders; it receives payment-settlement webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: Shopper accounts have not rolled out MFA.
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that receives orders from the storefront API, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The database password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)
data_stores.notes: The order service accesses it with a single application account that has full read/write.

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive
data_stores.notes: The receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.

data_flows.name: browse storefront
data_flows.description: A shopper browses the storefront through the storefront API.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: A shopper submits an order through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.notes: Shopper accounts have not rolled out MFA.
data_flows.data_description: order submission, including shopper and order information

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC
data_flows.notes: The order service accepts anything that can reach it; the text says there is no auth on this gRPC call.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values in the orders database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The account password comes from an environment variable on the worker.
data_flows.authentication: single application account; password from an environment variable

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket
data_flows.notes: The connection uses the order service's own service account.

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment to report that the order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: Authentication is unverified: the source says, "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone from which shoppers reach the storefront API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The internal network containing the order service and orders database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

trust_boundaries.name: Cloud Storage
trust_boundaries.description: The Cloud Storage hosting zone containing the receipt archive.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is the storefront API used by shoppers to browse the storefront and place orders.

assumptions.assumption: The order service is a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: Its caller reaches it through an RPC contract, specifically gRPC.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: Its stated contents include shopper addresses and card-last-four values, whose disclosure harms people or the business.

assumptions.assumption: The Cloud Storage receipt archive is in a separately controlled tenant zone.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a Cloud Storage bucket, a vendor-hosted storage service distinct from the core network.

assumptions.assumption: The Cloud Storage boundary is tenant-controlled rather than an internal network boundary.
assumptions.basis: Cloud Storage is a vendor-hosted service, so the named storage zone is controlled by a different party.
